content: In a tragic event, retired Army veteran Shamsuddin and his wife Saddo Begum were discovered murdered in their residence, the police alerted by neighbors. Their bodies were located amidst a pool of blood, prompting forensic experts and a dog squad to join the inquiry. With the motive still unknown, multiple investigation teams are being formed.

title: Panda-monium: When diplomacy goes to the dogs, horses, and elephants
content: Get ready, Atlanta! Two charming giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will be gracing the zoo with their presence this Monday, thanks to a decade-long conservation agreement. This unique event reflects the tradition of panda diplomacy, which has played a pivotal role in fostering international friendships. The nuances of this approach reveal essential lessons in both diplomacy and environmental conservation.

title: New Green Card rules from September: Categories affected and those exempt
content: Beginning in September 2026, the USCIS unveiled new regulations affecting Green Card seekers. These guidelines emphasize the financial self-sufficiency of applicants while excluding those in humanitarian categories. Nearly all applicants, including family and various occupational groups, must satisfy these criteria. While the Form I-864, Affidavit of Support, is crucial, it cannot guarantee approval on its own.

title: $17.1M to restore 206,000 acres, 225 miles for wildlife movement in West
content: The National Fish and Wildlife Foundation has announced $13.3 million in grants for 14 projects across the western US. With $3.8 million in matching contributions, the conservation work will have a total impact of $17.1 million. The projects will restore habitat, improve migration corridors and modify 225 miles of fencing for wildlife.

title: California buried 662,700 tires under I-880 ramp, saved $477K, 22 years
content: Engineers faced challenges while upgrading a highway interchange in Milpitas due to unstable bay mud. They opted to use shredded waste tires as lightweight fill to prevent ground settlement. This choice reduced weight on the soft soil by 40 percent and saved significant project costs. Over two decades, the infrastructure has shown no maintenance issues or structural damage.

title: Playing reef sounds underwater attracted 14x more baby fish in Hawai'i test
content: In an exciting breakthrough, scientists discovered that playing sounds from thriving coral reefs significantly draws in young fish larvae. The study conducted in Kāne‘ohe Bay revealed an uptick in larval presence at sites featuring these sound recordings. However, the increased attraction was transient. This pioneering research indicates that using natural soundscapes might support reef restoration efforts, highlighting the need for further investigation into the lasting impacts on fish populations.

title: Florida used robot rabbits to hunt Burmese pythons threatening the Everglades
content: Florida is testing solar-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades. Developed by the South Florida Water Management District and University of Florida, the robotic decoys mimic prey using heat and scent while AI cameras detect approaching snakes. Officials can then alert trained removal agents, adding technology to Florida’s wider python control efforts.

title: Rob Lowe says he was happy after Will Smith slapped Chris Rock at Oscars
content: Rob Lowe has revealed he was “the only person happy” when Will Smith slapped Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars, hoping the shocking incident would overshadow his infamous 1989 Academy Awards performance. Lowe joked that his decades-old Oscars blunder continues to haunt him, despite Smith’s slap becoming one of Hollywood’s biggest controversies.

title: Jason and Kylie Kelce’s investment reaches 5,000 stores in $2.9 billion move
content: Jason Kelce has made a savvy equity investment in Hank Sauce via Winnie Capital, marking a significant step for both him and the brand. Once a local staple, Hank Sauce now boasts distribution in over 5,000 stores across the country. With a U.S. hot sauce market worth nearly $2.9 billion, this partnership looks to amplify Hank Sauce's visibility and reach nationally, taking advantage of the substantial growth opportunities ahead.

title: Shohei Ohtani’s $700 million Dodgers contract and what it means for MLB
content: Shohei Ohtani’s $700 million contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers sounds like a blockbuster headline figure, but the deal is far more unusual than that. The deal shifted the Dodgers' payroll strategy with $680 million deferred until 2034-43, and Ohtani's commercial appeal drew major attention in Japan and around the world. The deal also helped to change how massive player contracts can be structured by MLB teams.

title: 3 killed, 4 injured after fight erupts into gunfire at Detroit strip club in US
content: Three individuals lost their lives while four others sustained injuries in a shooting at a Detroit strip club. The confrontation, which occurred early on Sunday morning, stemmed from an argument between several patrons. Detroit Police Chief Todd Bettison confirmed that the three deceased victims were all men. Authorities are actively investigating the case and have received multiple complaints about the venue this year.

title: Asian Games: Athletics leads India’s seven-medal haul, three boxers assure medals

Parul Chaudhary shone brightly, securing a bronze in the women’s 3000m steeplechase. Silver medals were added by Ancy Sojan and Sarvesh Kushare in their respective disciplines. The boxing team also excelled, confirming three medals through successful semifinal performances.

title: Nepal battered by severe rain: 21 dead, 5 missing as floods, landslides worsen
content: In Nepal, heavy rainfall has caused devastating floods and landslides, resulting in 21 lives lost and extensive damage. Authorities have evacuated around 3,000 residents from perilous areas to guarantee their safety. This deluge follows the earlier Bhotekoshi floods, which had a death toll of over 1,400. As rescue efforts continue, landslides have disrupted operations in several districts, and tourists in vulnerable areas are being advised to take precautions.

title: IndiGo A321 enroute Blr suffers tail strike; plane lands safely in second attempt

All passengers and crew were safely disembarked, and the aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is investigating the incident and has engaged with IndiGo regarding pilot training enhancements.

title: US rejects Iran's claim of capturing underwater drone, calls move 'desperate'

In response, the US military dismissed this assertion, clarifying that the drone in question had experienced a malfunction prior to any claims from Iran. This development follows Iran's earlier announcement regarding another US military drone capture.

title: '40km chase': Cop clings to speeding car to catch smugglers in Coimbatore; watch

title: IndiGo A321 suffers tail strike in Bengaluru
content:
An IndiGo A321 operating flight 6E 6542 from Guwahati to Bengaluru suffered a tail strike while aborting its landing on Sunday.

NEW DELHI: In yet another instance of an IndiGo Airbus A321 tail strike, an aircraft (VT-NHP) operating a Guwahati-Bengaluru flight Sunday suffered one while going around at its destination. Flight 6E 6542 aborted landing in its first approach. While making an ascent, it suffered a tail strike. The aircraft landed safely in its second attempt. DGCA has launched a probe. An IndiGo spokesperson said the flight experienced "abnormal runway contact" while landing during gusty weather at Kempegowda International Airport, adding, "All customers and crew are safe... All relevant authorities were info-rmed and the aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks."

title: Bank unions call off 3-day strike after assurances, IBA to study demands
content:
Bank unions withdraw three-day strike after late-night agreement with IBA on key demands.

NEW DELHI: Bank unions called off their proposed three-day strike just before midnight after the Indian Banks Association agreed to look into their demands. "A high-level committee of IBA and UFBU (United Forum of Bank Unions) will be formed immediately to deliberate on the issue of declaring the remaining Saturdays as holidays. This committee will explore, all possible alternatives; discuss with all stakeholders, and work out a solution acceptable to all stakeholders and, more importantly, the customers," a late night communication said. Unions want a five-day work week, which is being resisted by banks as it may inconvenience customers. The late-night announcement came after what turned out to be a working Sunday for state-run bank employees as govt ordered branches to stay open so that customers are not inconvenienced.
